summary: 8 targeted claims: 4 stronger-original (C1 job-board mechanic, C6 screen-aversion exists, C7 Sept/Jan windows now corroborated by Lifeway 2025, C8 vendor figures as hedged); 2 stronger-counter on the contested point (C2 faith.tools audience is small, superlative outweighed; C5 fragmentation fatigue is vendor-asserted and unmeasured); 1 split (C3: free tier removes the cost objection, but SmartGroups' 15 iOS ratings mean it is not a benchmark to match); 1 unresolved (C4 teacher-champion mapping; turnover risk carried forward, motivation argument retired). Original claims disproven: 1 as worded only (C5 'documented'). Original claims false: 0. Counter arguments failing outright: 3 (C8 discrepancy is a conceded units mismatch plus irrelevant market-size spread; C3 conflates objection-removal with conversion; C4 motivation argument cuts the other way) plus C1's overstated 'wrong feed' conclusion. Reclassifications: vendor customer bases move from identification mechanic to market-size context; faith.tools moves from 'most actionable reach item' to zero-cost hygiene listing. 7 open sub-questions carried forward, plus brief open questions #3, #8, #9 that no stage addressed. Steps 2, 4, 8 and the privacy/doctrinal rows were never targeted and stand as sourced-but-untested.
